title: Add Animated Focus Tree SVG Inside Timer Circle + Forest Mode

requirements.text: Create a new React component `FocusTree` (frontend/src/components/PomodoroTimer/FocusTree.tsx) that renders a minimal, aesthetic SVG illustration of a growing focus tree. The SVG must be centered behind the time digits inside the ProgressRing circle, using absolute positioning so it does not shift or obscure the countdown numbers or session label. The tree must look clean and modern (not cartoonish) — use simple geometric SVG paths for trunk, branches, and foliage. Apply a soft green neon glow effect (filter: drop-shadow) using a green accent color (e.g., #22c55e or #4ade80) at low opacity so it does not overpower the timer digits. The component must accept a `progress` prop (number 0–100) representing how much of the current focus session has elapsed.

quotes: Inside the circular timer, place a minimal animated "Focus Tree".
Tree should be centered behind the time digits.
Tree should look clean and aesthetic (not cartoonish).
Use SVG illustration for smooth scaling.

acceptanceCriteria: FocusTree component exists at frontend/src/components/PomodoroTimer/FocusTree.tsx
SVG tree is rendered using clean geometric paths (not raster or emoji)
Tree is absolutely positioned and centered behind the countdown digits inside the timer circle
Tree does not obscure or overlap the MM:SS countdown digits or session label
Soft green neon glow (drop-shadow filter) is applied to the SVG tree shape
Component accepts a `progress` prop (0–100)

requirements.text: Implement the growth animation logic for the FocusTree component. The tree's visual state must transition smoothly through five growth stages based on the `progress` prop: 0% → seed (tiny dot or sprout shape), 25% → small plant (short stem with small leaves), 50% → medium plant (taller stem, more foliage), 75% → almost full tree (branching structure), 100% → fully grown glowing tree (complete canopy with intensified neon glow). Use CSS keyframe transitions or SVG attribute interpolation (via React state/style) so growth animation is smooth and lag-free. The tree must not jump between stages abruptly — interpolate SVG path scales or opacity smoothly. Do not use any heavy animation libraries.
acceptanceCriteria: At progress=0, only a seed/sprout shape is visible
At progress=25, a small plant with a short stem is visible
At progress=50, a medium-height plant with more foliage is visible
At progress=75, a branched tree close to full size is visible
At progress=100, the fully grown tree is visible with an intensified neon glow
Transitions between stages are smooth (no abrupt jumps)
Animation uses only CSS transitions or lightweight SVG interpolation — no heavy third-party animation libraries

requirements.text: Wire the FocusTree component to the Pomodoro timer state in PomodoroTimer.tsx and usePomodoroTimer.ts. Compute the `progress` value as the percentage of elapsed time within the current focus session: `progress = ((focusDurationSeconds - remainingSeconds) / focusDurationSeconds) * 100`, clamped to 0–100. When the timer is running, the tree grows in real time as time elapses. When the timer is paused, the tree freezes at its current growth stage (do not animate while paused). When the timer reset button is pressed, the tree must reset back to the seed stage (progress = 0). The tree must only grow during focus sessions — do not advance the tree during break sessions.

quotes: Tree slowly grows as time passes.
Do not reset unless timer reset button is pressed.

acceptanceCriteria: Tree progress increases in real time as the focus timer counts down
Tree is frozen (does not animate) when the timer is paused
Pressing the reset button resets the tree to seed stage (progress = 0)
Tree does not grow during break sessions
Progress calculation is correct: 0% at session start, 100% when focus session completes

requirements.text: Integrate the FocusTree SVG into the ProgressRing component (frontend/src/components/PomodoroTimer/ProgressRing.tsx). The tree must be rendered inside the SVG or as an absolutely positioned element inside the timer circle container, layered behind the countdown text (z-index below the time digits). The tree must not be rendered in the Streamer Mode variant (280px size) on the /timer route — only render it in the default/dashboard size variant. Ensure the tree SVG scales proportionally within the circle diameter so it fills the inner area attractively without clipping.

requirements.text: Apply responsive sizing to the FocusTree SVG component. On mobile viewports (below sm/md breakpoint), the tree must be slightly smaller so it fits comfortably inside the smaller timer circle. On desktop viewports, the tree should be larger and more prominent. Use Tailwind responsive classes or CSS viewport/clamp units to achieve this. The tree must always remain centered inside the timer circle on all screen sizes.
acceptanceCriteria: On mobile viewports, the tree is proportionally smaller than on desktop
On desktop viewports, the tree is larger and visually prominent
Tree remains perfectly centered inside the timer circle on both mobile and desktop
Tree never overflows or clips outside the timer circle boundary

requirements.text: Implement Forest Mode: each time a Pomodoro focus session completes (not a break session), add one small tree icon to a 'Forest' display area shown below the main timer on the dashboard (route '/'). Display the accumulated trees as small tree emojis or minimal SVG tree icons (e.g., 🌲) in a row/wrap layout, with a label showing the daily tree count (e.g., 'Today's Forest: 🌲🌲🌲 3 trees'). Persist the daily tree count in localStorage using a date-keyed entry (reset to 0 automatically at the start of a new calendar day). Forest Mode display must only appear on the dashboard in non-Streamer, non-Study-Mode views — hide it entirely in Streamer Mode and Study Mode.

All new labels and text in the Forest Mode section must be in English. The tree and forest elements must not interfere with the existing timer controls, settings panels, motivational quote, or 'Stay Locked In.' text.
